A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScalingAR and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The changed title, formatting, and appendix organization do not prevent reliable content matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original ScalingAR benchmark evaluations, component ablations, a 15-participant user study, and robustness and sensitivity results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations on two more base models, policy ablations, computational measurements, and entropy analyses.

M1.justification: The same confidence channels, pruning mechanism, and guidance scheduler remain. However, v2 specifies a running-minimum pruning trigger and separate absolute/relative recovery tests, while v3 uses current confidence and a simplified relative-rebound test. Algorithm 1 also omits the recovery window still documented elsewhere. These inconsistencies prevent distinguishing an actual procedural revision from an abbreviated description.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image generation using GenEval, TIIF-Bench, and image-suitable IPV-TXT impossible prompts. The additional base models and qualitative examples in v3 do not establish new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds unmodified SimpleAR and Janus-Pro as direct controls against their ScalingAR variants. Table 1 retains its comparator membership, including the original Janus entry, and IS and BoN remain the conventional scaling baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations with SimpleAR-1.5B and Janus-Pro-1B and a GenEval profiling experiment on H200 hardware measuring latency, FLOPs, and memory with specified candidate counts. Changes to the retained benchmark or user-study protocols are not established; newly disclosed baseline settings are documentation additions.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supplementary analysis with separate termination-only and scheduler-only ablations (Table 4), computational overhead profiling (Table 5), spatial entropy visualizations (Figure 7), and local confidence-weight sensitivity tests (Figure 11). The earlier global-weight and recovery-threshold analyses remain as Figures 9–10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce a new statistical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results: Table 3 reports base/ScalingAR GenEval overall scores of 0.63/0.67 for SimpleAR and 0.73/0.77 for Janus-Pro, alongside new policy, computational, and sensitivity outcomes. Table 2 changes the overall score without Token-Level Confidence from 42.9 to 40.4. Table 1 and the existing figures' results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes some explicit mathematical specification: v2's entropy/margin combination and clipped conditional-score mapping become unspecified normalization descriptions, and its bounded, smoothed guidance-update equation is absent. The autoregressive preliminaries and rebound definition remain. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion soften 'the first' NTP scaling framework to 'a novel' framework, although Section 2 retains a first-strategy claim. The two-level contribution, first exploration of visual token entropy, and headline performance, efficiency, and robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit entropy-as-risk qualification, an active-correction versus passive-selection explanation for outperforming BoN, and deployment boundaries concerning inherited biases and absent content filtering. Existing limitations are retained. Its new weight interpretation is inconsistent: Appendix D.2 calls 0.7/0.3 optimal, while Figure 11 peaks at 0.5/0.5.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises reproducibility information through Algorithm 1, a universal-configuration statement, entropy/margin weights, and ImageReward, N=8, and default-CFG baseline disclosures. It identifies H200 hardware for profiling but drops several earlier fill-ratio, calibration, protection-horizon, hard-fail, and guidance-safeguard specifications. The repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations on entropy calibration and high-entropy reasoning, plus SimpleAR, Janus-Pro, and ImageReward, while removing several tangential video-model references. Most related-work discussion and the positioning against TTS-VAR remain, with limited softening of priority wording.

P1.justification: The title and abstract change, and Section 4 is extensively rewritten from detailed operational definitions toward explanatory prose. The appendices are reorganized to separate implementation, additional models, and analysis. v3 also adds an Impact Statement and removes the LLM-use appendix.

P2.justification: v3 converts the main text and references to a two-column layout, extensively relocates displays, restructures the hyperparameter table, and adds three figures, three numbered tables, and Algorithm 1. Existing figures are retained under matched numbering rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The additional model evaluations, policy ablations, and measured latency/memory results in Tables 3–5 strengthen v2's evidence for generalization, component contributions, and practical efficiency. Baseline disclosures also help reproducibility. These gains are tempered by less explicit method specification and the new disagreement between Figure 11 and its interpretation, supporting a limited net improvement.
